title: Armenia
subtitle: to the shores of Lake Sevan
standfirst: A decade on, I’m looking back at a week in August 2015 through the photographs I took: up through Syunik, east into Karabakh, back over the Sotk Pass to Lake Sevan, and on to Yerevan. Some of these places are unchanged. Some no longer exist as I saw them.

cover.alt: Sevanavank's stone church silhouetted at sunset above Lake Sevan

music.title: À la côte de la mer de Gegham
music.blurb: A piece about Lake Sevan, for wind band.

stops.caption: The first stop, and the first photographs of the week. Kapan sits in the Voghji valley below Mount Khustup.

photos.alt: The Voghji river running through Kapan beneath a building that spans it, forested ridges behind
A huge stone equestrian monument above the road, a white Lada driving past
A hand-painted shop sign in Armenian script hanging from a stone wall

stops.caption: A Soviet-era square under the rock pinnacles of Old Goris. From here the road ran east through the Lachin corridor into Karabakh. The road is still there; the journey it made is not.

photos.alt: Cliffs riddled with cave dwellings rising above the end of a Goris street
The main square of Goris with ornate lamp posts, under a peak of rock pinnacles
A stone doorway under a sign reading House of Veterans in Armenian and Russian, with a hammer and sickle
A boy walks past the arched stone war-memorial fountain, its frieze carved with Armenian lettering
A row of patched garages with rusting roofs under walnut trees
A statue between two columns on a square, parked cars in front and mountains behind

stops.caption: In 2015 this was the capital of an unrecognised Armenian republic, with the 1967 monument We Are Our Mountains on the hill above. Since 2023 it has been Khankendi, under Azerbaijani control, and nearly all of its Armenian residents have left.

photos.alt: The red tufa monument We Are Our Mountains, two giant stone faces on a grassy hill, visitors taking photos
A lamp-lined boulevard at sunset leading to a pale stone public building
A small jewellery-repair kiosk with signs in Armenian and Russian, apartment blocks behind
A white Lada rounding a square beneath a statue on a tall plinth, cypress trees behind
A guesthouse room in morning light: striped runner on a red-painted floor, ferns, stacked bedding

stops.caption: Gandzasar monastery, consecrated in 1240. Of everything on this road, it has seen the most borders come and go.

photos.alt: The carved drum and conical roof of Gandzasar church against a blue sky
The long rubble-stone monastery wall with arched wooden doors and small windows

stops.caption: Back into Armenia over the Sotk Pass and down to Vardenis. Since 2020 the land on the far side of the pass has been Azerbaijani.

photos.alt: Cattle standing and lying on a gravel mountain road between forested slopes
Soviet apartment blocks with washing on the balconies, a wide plain and mountains behind

stops.caption: Sevanavank, on a peninsula that was an island until the lake was lowered in the Soviet era. Of the whole week, this is the place I came back to, nine years later, in music.

photos.alt: Sevanavank's church above Lake Sevan in evening light, a man walking towards a camera on a tripod

stops.caption: The end of the Armenian leg, with Ararat to the south on a clear morning. From here the road went north to Tbilisi.

photos.alt: People sitting on a stone parapet at the top of the Cascade, looking over Yerevan to the twin peaks of Ararat
An overgrown Soviet-era terraced fountain park with bronze figures and three arches
A seated bronze statue before the colonnaded Opera House
A wide avenue of pink-stone apartment blocks under a genocide-centenary billboard, a yellow bus in traffic
A suburban street of houses and vines, the TV tower on the hills beyond
A carved orange stone frieze of musicians and poets on a building beneath a sweeping roof
Visitors beside the eternal flame inside the ring of leaning basalt slabs at Tsitsernakaberd
A boy riding a wave board past the fan-shaped stone fountains of the Cascade
